chapter_plans.title: The Room That Would Not Warm
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Nora Vance inherits Agnes's shuttered seaside hotel, finds the salt room impossibly cold, and hears a child's voice say her name on an old tape.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Nora arrives at the inherited hotel with keys, legal papers, and the discipline of a sound restorer trying to treat grief as inventory; the first pressure point comes when the salt room stays cold despite the rest of the building holding normal stale warmth. While cataloging Agnes's preserved reel-to-reel equipment, Nora finds a tape labeled only with a date from the summer she turned seven and, after cleaning the heads, hears static resolve into a child's voice saying, 'Nora.' In the middle of the dread, Nora almost calls a solicitor, a locksmith, anyone living who could confirm the sound was real, then stops because the empty corridor and Agnes's old notes make the isolation worse: the evidence knows her, and no witness can share the burden yet. End with the tape capturing a second breath under Nora's own.
chapter_plans.opens_with: "Don't play that one after dark," the dead woman's handwriting warned from the tape box.
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: The restored tape catches Nora whispering, 'I didn't go in there,' followed by a child's voice answering from the static, 'You did.'
chapter_plans.chapter_task: Write 1600-1900 words. Open on the warning label, keep the prose hook-driven and concrete, establish Nora's analytical voice, the hotel, the cold salt room, Agnes's tapes, and the first recorded voice. Include quiet dread, one practical investigation sequence, and one vulnerable isolation beat centered on Nora needing a living witness but finding none. Do not introduce a romantic subplot, male lead, flirtation, or romantic counterpart.
must_happen: Nora takes legal possession of Agnes Vance's shuttered seaside hotel and begins treating the building as evidence rather than home.
She discovers the salt room remains unnaturally cold after confirming nearby rooms are not, using practical checks instead of accepting a haunting explanation.
Nora finds Agnes's reel-to-reel machine and a tape dated from Nora's seventh summer, then restores enough audio to hear a child's voice say her name.
Nora nearly calls a solicitor, locksmith, or any practical living witness after the voice comes through, but stops when the empty corridor makes clear she has no one present to verify what she heard.
A dry windowsill inside the cold room shows salt crust arranged in a shape like tiny finger marks, though the window has been sealed for years.

Do not show Della visually or let any supernatural voice speak live outside recorded sound.

Do not introduce an actual male love interest, absent male lead marker, flirtation, romantic subplot, or any named romantic counterpart.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: A brass hotel key tagged with a brittle strip of seaweed pressed flat under old varnish, labeled in Agnes's handwriting: SALT ROOM — DO NOT WARM.
chapter_plans.carries_to_next: Nora has the tape, proof that the room and the recording know something she does not, and a reason to search Agnes's catalog for more reels from the same summer.

chapter_plans.title: Two Breaths on One Tape
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Nora cleans the first recording, finds evidence of two children breathing on it, and learns Ruth lied about what was kept from Agnes's house.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Nora spends the morning after the first impossible playback restoring the damaged reel in Agnes's cold hotel, separating hiss, room tone, tape warp, and voiceprint with the same discipline she uses on other people's evidence. The work turns intimate and frightening when the cleaned file reveals two distinct child-breath patterns beneath the spoken fragments, though Nora refuses to call that proof of twins and records it only as an unexplained acoustic anomaly. Ruth phones before Nora can ask directly, warning her not to sleep in the hotel and insisting Agnes kept nothing worth preserving; Nora compares that denial to the shelves of labeled tapes, the working recorder, and Agnes's meticulous storage index, hearing the family lie forming in real time. In the dangerous quiet after Ruth hangs up, Nora nearly reaches for her phone from the old human urge to have anyone witness fear, then stops because there is no safe witness here except the evidence. The chapter pays off the first tape with a concrete new clue to the tidal pool while withholding the twin answer.

chapter_plans.cliffhanger: When Nora rewinds the warped lullaby one final time, the scraped index entry turns legible for half a second and shows a single word beside the missing reel number: "POOL."

chapter_plans.title: The Pool Tape
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Nora follows Agnes's damaged index to the tidal pool, finds a hidden reel sealed in salt-stiff cloth, and hears a child's recording count down to something she cannot remember.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Nora searches the hotel using Agnes's index and the word 'POOL,' moving from the salt room and tape archive toward the tidal pool outside the shuttered building. The path does not feel new to her body: her shoes hesitate at a broken flagstone before her mind can explain why, and the sound of water in the rock basin makes her count under her breath without meaning to. At the pool, she finds a salt-stiff cloth packet wedged behind a loose stone, containing a small reel that Agnes hid away from the main archive. Back inside, Nora plays only a fragment before the machine threatens to chew the tape: two children count seconds, one giggles, and one says Nora's name as if warning her. In the pressure of handling evidence that seems to know her better than she knows herself, Nora has a brief vulnerable beat of wanting a steady human witness, but there is no safe person to call, only the tape and the empty hotel. End with Ruth proving she knows exactly what Nora removed from the pool.
chapter_plans.opens_with: "If this tape snaps, whatever Agnes hid dies twice," Nora whispered.
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Ruth's message plays through Nora's phone speaker: 'Put back what you took from the pool before it starts calling you by the other name.'
